aboutPage.title: A home for micronational knowledge
aboutPage.intro: It's hard to tell when the actual concept of The Micronational Directory was conceived, because we can say it existed as a fantasy prior to its proper development. Although, the creation per se occurred during the first days of August 2023, and not so long after (specifically on August 31) the platform had its official launch for the first beta version.
aboutPage.team: Our team is composed of a few micronationalists (that also happen to be web developers), guided and encouraged by the same spirit that most other micronationalists have: an inexplicable thirst for knowing more and more about these political phenomena that we all contribute to create. But it's not just about that on itself — it's also for having a complete, accurate, scalable, accessible, universal and perpetual resource for recording all that knowledge. And that's where we've decided to come in, because TMD aims no purpose other than that.
aboutPage.mission: Yes, it sounds very bold, and there are different platforms that serve a similar function. But they can't guarantee all those concepts at once. And given the basis this Directory is founded on, we think we may achieve the totality of what is necessary to guarantee that. Using the framework Vue.js 3 and Google Firebase for handling the data, the result is a robust, fast and modern webapp that provides the user with a fluid dynamic for searching any micronation in a single place. And what better decision than sharing the power with our aforementioned peers from this community — we can all participate here in registering our inventions: the micronations of yesterday, today and tomorrow, and no matter where from. Be sure to leave your mark!

donatePage.intro: Since The Micronational Directory is an independent project without any sponsors, it is funded entirely by the personal income of our team, who also run the website in their free time. Here are the services we use and the expenses we pay each month:
donatePage.vercel: Vercel: This provider hosts our Vue.js webapp and makes it accessible to everyone online. Vercel provides TMD's base URL (https://the-micronational-directory.vercel.app/). We currently have no costs for this service, but that may change in the future.
donatePage.nic: Nic.ar: Argentina's official domain registrar. We acquired a custom domain for our webapp, likely the address you used to access this site. It costs approximately 1 USD per year.
donatePage.firebase: Google Firebase: This backend stores and processes information about micronation entries, user accounts and contests. It provides databases, authentication and flag storage. Usage-based costs are currently low (around 0.10 USD per month) but may rise as traffic and usage grow.
donatePage.mapbox: Mapbox: We use this service for maps when adding a physical micronation or viewing all entries on the globe. The free plan covers a monthly number of map loads that our current traffic has not exceeded, though this may change.
donatePage.emailjs: EmailJS: We mainly use this service to send authors automatic emails when their submissions are approved or rejected, along with other notices. The free plan is limited to 200 emails per month and is not enough. The basic paid plan costs 9 USD per month, and we are considering it.

home.heroCopy: Discover the micronations and organizations shaping our community, across the world and throughout history.
home.heroTagline: The way it was always meant to be.
home.postsUnavailable: Updates couldn’t load. View the account on X ↗
home.introContent:
Micronations are particular political phenomena that have existed for decades and, arguably, centuries. They may be founded for many reasons and aspire to a long and active legacy. Some cases are linked to ethnic or social conflicts; others demonstrate political debate and experimentation. There are also fraudulent schemes, exercises of imagination or ambition, and even jokes. Whatever their origin, they share a common root: their founders and citizens "[...] claim that they belong to an independent nation or sovereign state, but which lacks legal recognition by world governments or major international organizations [...]", as Wikipedia describes.

These small political entities are scattered around the world—not only on Earth, but also in digital spaces, and sometimes with territorial claims over other planets and space. They also span a wide range of time: some were founded in the 19th century, while social media today provide a home for many virtual micronations.

The goal of The Micronational Directory team is to build the most complete and unified list of micronations possible: a shared database that brings entries together regardless of their characteristics or criteria. This site does not aim to debate or describe each case in depth; other established platforms already serve that purpose, such as MicroWiki and Micro Flag Archive. Let’s build this together and create the place our community deserves.

newEntry.title: Important notes on new entries and how to add your own
newEntry.resourceIntro: Don’t know what micronations to add?
newEntry.resourceLink: Check out this list of sources we compiled
newEntry.content:
We invite the community to contribute entries to the directory. Please keep the following in mind:

  • Provide true, appropriate, and precise information. Entries promoting Nazi symbols, adult content, or illegal activity will be rejected.
  • Submitted micronations and organizations must have at least one month of proven existence. This helps us avoid short-lived entries that may be games or premature experiments.
  • Every entry must include a website source and/or, preferably, a wiki article. This lets us verify the information and avoid jokes, games, fake or misleading entries, and contest cheating.
  • Physical and digital micronations are welcome. Fictional countries may be included if they show activity as a micronation, such as news, diplomacy, or community activity. Babar’s Kingdom is not a valid case, while the Kingdom of Redonda and many micronations from Micras are.
  • Whenever possible, enter the information in English; otherwise, use the micronation’s or organization’s main official language.
  • If a website is inactive, check the Wayback Machine for an archived version that can be used as a source.
  • All submissions require administrator approval, which can take up to 72 hours, before appearing in the public directory.

Thanks for helping us build this digital archive!

entryTooltips: This should be the most common, shortest variant of the name, barely the proper name itself. Take 'Sealand', 'Hutt River' or 'Denmark' as examples. Ideally, use the main official language version or an English one if available.

Here, the descriptive rest of the full name's composition should be added, excluding the main name added above. Barely 'Principality of' or 'Republic of' are some examples of proper cases. There may be some cases, like 'Athenian Republic', in which this field remains blank and only 'Name' is filled. Avoid adding 'The' and words that serve the same meaning at the beginning.
Other official or commonly used names, including names in other languages. Add the corresponding title when applicable.
Same as 'Title', but input it in another language. To follow above's example, 'Respubliko de la' could be placed here.

Official, national motto. Be sure to NOT add quotes of any kind. The proper way to populate the field is placing the motto in whatever language it is, and then adding the English translation between parenthesis if available. For instance, a valid input is: Vivat Rex (Long Live the King).

The 'Type' of the micronation applies in regard of its kind of (non) territorial claim. Micronations that claim territory on Earth or other real-world elements are 'Physical', the ones that exist solely on the Internet and don't have actual land pretensions are 'Digital', while cases that live on simulated or fantasy worlds are 'Fictional'. More than one type can be checked, for sure.

Official languages spoken. Can be also extended to other national and/or recognized languages. If there isn't any, place the de facto language or the one used by representatives on websites and social media.
Physical, digital or fictional city or any kind of place officiating as the micronation's capital. If there's more than one, then add all of them separated by commas.

Currency (or currencies) legally adopted and accepted, they could be purported as well, either physical and digital. Some micronations even include macronational fiat currencies, and they are applicable as well. If there's more than one, then add all of them separated by commas. DO NOT include their symbols between parenthesis, e.g. (K$).

The full foundation date. If there's not enough information to input a full date, select the first day of the available timespan data and mark data as uncertain. For instance, if it's only known that it was founded on 1997, input January 1, 1997. If a foundation is stated on August, 2004, select August 1, 2004.

The micronation's location of its territorial claims. There is no possibility for selecting polygonal ranges, only geopoint pins. So, for large territorial claims, you can mark the capital or even the leader's approximate location. In any case not applicable, just leave the blue pin as is.

Supramicronational organizations that this micronation is currently a member of AND also was a member of in the past. There is no possibility to indicate membership type, so full members, partial members, observer members and any other kind of distinctive cases should be added alike. On the 'Other' subfield you can add organizations that are not present on our directory, and also the main name of another micronation in case this one is a constituent country/nation.

Any communication media should be added here. This includes email addresses, social media profiles (adding the full URL, not just the username), links to chat or group invitation, forums and other similar platforms.

Complete the field by adding websites that contain relevant info. This should always include official websites (if available), wiki or news articles, and unofficial websites where data was gathered from. If you come across a dead website, check it out using https://web.archive.org/ and if there is a saved snapshot, add its link here instead.

Upload an image or provide a direct image URL. Images are compressed in their original format to fit within the ~35 KB limit. In the majority of cases, the national flag should be chosen here, but it could be that the State flag or even civil flag is the prevalent one. There is no possibility for adding more than one flag (e.g. co-official flags), so the most prevalent one should be added. Always add the latest and current version.
